session.title: 1.0.45 released: accounts by company, plan accounts used where you choose, balance monitors, every action on the control routes; 1.0.44 taken down
session.purpose: SW309 from a worker brief: the user rejected 1.0.44's coding plans as Claude Code/OpenCode presets. Through several rounds he set the direction: Switchy manages subscription accounts by company, the program an account runs in is a 'Used in' setting on its card, pay-as-you-go keys are monitor-only (balance and spend), relays stay with the company whose program they serve, the card mirrors how each company records usage, and every window and tray action must be reachable through the control routes. Also: take down the published 1.0.44, then release 1.0.45.
outcomes: 1.0.44 taken down (c581c84b): GitHub release v1.0.44 with exe, msi and DMG, the v1.0.44 tag, the DMG build artifact, and its three commits on the public repo (main back to 3546abac50) deleted; private main kept its history; scripts/publish_public.sh leaves 1.0.44's three installer files out of the public copy; CHANGELOG marks 1.0.44 withdrawn.

1.0.45 (8fe6e55c): the sidebar lists companies (Claude, OpenAI, Google, Kimi, Cursor, Z.ai GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, OpenCode, Command Code; Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud, BytePlus, StepFun once they hold an account; Other for pay-as-you-go keys run in a program). Program sign-ins and relays serving a program sit under its company; Settings > Programs holds each program's account in use, proxy/failover switches, Oh My OpenCode profiles and OpenClaw. 'API key' is gone from the UI.

Plan accounts are rows of the new accounts table (schema v8); 'Used in' makes an ordinary provider of the program from src/config/planPrograms.json (generated from the catalog and presets by tests/config/planPrograms.test.ts) linked by meta.accountId. A Kimi Code console key is optional on its sign-in card. Balance monitors read DeepSeek, Moonshot and StepFun balances; spend is counted from drops between readings (balance_readings). The v8 migration ran on the workstation: 0 accounts, 0 providers linked (the workstation holds only sign-ins).

Usage: OpenCode Go reads zen/go/v1/usage (5-hour, weekly, monthly; its usage call has no per-model figures, reported to the user); Command Code fixed (windowLimits is top-level, the 1.0.44 parser looked one level too deep) and adds the month's plan credits and extra credits.

Control routes: audit of 146 window actions plus tray and route rows (docs/control_routes_audit_2026_10_25.md); fixed the theme (frontend-only), the tray's Show and Quit (no command), exit_lightweight_mode refused while the window was closed, and Used in built in the window; new add_sign_in_account, use_account_in, remove_account_from, get_account_quota, show_main_window, quit_app, set_window_appearance. README has a recipe per company. Verified on the installed build with throwaway entries: the Z.ai recipe end to end (save, use in OpenCode, quota, key change reaching opencode.json, Codex refused, remove, delete) and add_sign_in_account for Cursor and Kimi (deleted, never switched); capture_claude_account is dispatched over the route (answers its own 'Provider ... not found'); a real capture was not run to avoid overwriting a stored login. The switchy_account_signin skill's 'no HTTP route' line was corrected in all four copies (hashes match).

Checks: pnpm typecheck and vitest 176/176; cargo test 798/799, the failure being the proxy test that needs port 15721, which the installed Switchy holds; the public repo's CI passed both suites on 1.0.45 (run 40239506892). Installed 1.0.45 on the workstation and checked on screen: company sidebar with in-use dots, Claude and OpenAI pages ('Used in Codex' after the fix for a pooled program the proxy has not served yet), a plan card with Used in OpenCode, a balance monitor card. An install started while the stopped copy was still exiting left the old exe; the README now says to wait until no switchy process is left.

Released 1.0.45 as 1.0.44 was: private origin pushed, public copy via scripts/publish_public.sh, macOS DMG from build-macos.yml (run 40239539965), GitHub release v1.0.45 (Latest) with exe, msi and DMG; DMG committed in installers/ (d3558f14). SW309 done with refs 8fe6e55c and d3558f14; the brief is in brief_archive/.
session.latest_summary: 1.0.45 released: accounts by company with Used in per program, plan accounts and balance monitors, every action reachable over the control routes; 1.0.44 taken down.

current_focus.summary: Switchy 1.0.45 is released (GitHub Latest, Windows installers and Apple Silicon DMG) and runs on the workstation: the sidebar lists companies, each account card shows its usage the way the company records it and a Used in row for the programs it runs in, pay-as-you-go keys are balance monitors, and every window and tray action is reachable through POST /switchy/invoke (README 'Control routes', recipe per company). 1.0.44 was taken down. The laptop has 1.0.40 with Switchy quit; another user's PC and Mac have 1.0.39. Await the user's feedback on the new layout; the confirmations below stay pending under their triggers.

next_actions.summary: CONFIRM THE CRASH RESTART ON THE NEXT REAL CRASH (1.0.40). After any Switchy crash on the workstation: Application log event 1000 for switchy.exe, then within about a minute a new switchy.log starting with '[crash_restart] Windows will restart Switchy after a crash or hang' and the proxy on 15721 without a manual start; switchy.prev.log ends at the crash; ~/.switchy/crash.log gains an [ABNORMAL EXIT] entry naming the exception, any 'Windows ran out of memory' line and the dump path. A restart that did not happen while commit was still exhausted is the known single-attempt limit (finding doc option 2 is the backstop).

Confirm account-proxy coverage on the next natural Claude sign-in or renewal while Owen is selected, without forcing a new login. Claude Code's own exchange should log '[connect_tunnel] platform.claude.com:443 via socks5://82.26.163.142:45001'. For Switchy's renewal, observe '[claude_pool] refreshing login for provider=98e00f12...' and the successful refreshed-login message; the enforced per-account client route is owned by proxy/http_client.rs. Windows/WSL HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY, UK exit probes and telemetry tunnels were verified; a live sign-in/renewal using this route remains unobserved. Connection failures must stop rather than fall back to direct; country observations only warn.

CONFIRM THE RESTART PATH ON STEPHEN'S NEXT WINDOWS RESTART (1.0.29). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.prev.log after 'Session ending; handing the live configs back': '[session-end] claude/codex/gemini handed back', '[session-end] ... in WSL handed back', then 'Live configs handed back for the session end'. 'did not finish in 4 seconds' with the last [session-end] line shows which step stalls (Windows step = database lock, WSL step = WSL I/O); fix that step. In switchy.log: Switchy started within seconds of login (window hidden, launched with --autostart from HKCU Run), '[auto_launch] start at login on', proxy on 15721, and Claude Code / Codex answer without ECONNREFUSED.

CONFIRM CLAUDE LOGINS STAY IN STEP WITH WSL (1.0.27). In switchy.log, when an account WSL is signed in to renews: '[claude_pool] provider=... took the newer login from WSL' or 'wrote the refreshed login through to WSL', and no new 'invalid_grant' 'Refresh token not found or invalid' in account_switches/provider_health. WSL's ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.switchy/accounts/<id>/credentials.json for that account should carry the same refreshToken after each renewal.

CONFIRM ROTATION AND CODEX FAILOVER ON LIVE TRAFFIC (1.0.25/1.0.26). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log and the switchy.db account_switches table: (a) when an account's five-hour window resets while another serves, a switch back to it with reason 'recovered' and detail "Another account's weekly limit resets sooner"; (b) a Codex turn refused for usage that continues an earlier one logs '[CodexWS] provider=... websocket closed (turn refused for usage; Codex resends it in full)' and the turn then completes on the next account with no error in Codex. GET http://127.0.0.1:15721/switchy/accounts shows current account, pool order, quota and atLimit per account.

VERIFY LOCAL PROXY OFF WITH AN OPEN CODEX WINDOW. the user was asked to turn Local proxy off in Settings > Pool, then use a Codex window opened while the proxy was on. Confirm in C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log that "Proxy turned off; its listener stays up..." was logged, that the Codex window's later [Codex] requests still reached the proxy and answered, that netstat shows 127.0.0.1:15721 still LISTENING, and that Settings shows the proxy as off. Turning it back on must reuse the listener.

QUIT CASE WAITS ON STEPHEN. Quitting Switchy still breaks Codex windows opened under the proxy. He was offered a warning on quit naming the open Codex windows (small) or running the proxy as a process that outlives Switchy's window (large); he has not chosen. Build nothing until he does.
If the user directs request logging to be enabled, first make the Usage page's Turn on button apply to the running proxy, then enable it for Claude, Codex, and Gemini.

CONFIRM CURSOR/ANTIGRAVITY ON THE NEXT REAL SIGN-IN (1.0.43). No sign-in was run to test, and only one account of each exists. When the user adds a second account: enable the new empty card, open a NEW PowerShell, sign in. Expect: cursor-agent login prints 'Open a browser and navigate to this link' and opens no browser (user env NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1); agy started signed out shows its link with a code field and opens no browser (the profile function from ~/.switchy/manual_sign_in/agy_sign_in.ps1 sets SSH_CLIENT only when cmdkey lists no gemini:antigravity entry). Then switch back to the first card: switchy.log shows no '[cursor_account]'/'[antigravity_account] live login (...) is not the account' refusal for a normal switch, cursor-agent status and agy's log name the first account, and each card keeps its own email and usage badge ('[...] usage of provider=... N windows' lines). Kimi Code still opens the default browser (README limitation).

CONFIRM PLAN ACCOUNTS AND BALANCE MONITORS ON THE FIRST REAL KEY (1.0.45, SW309). Nothing was subscribed; plan quota, balance and Used in were checked only with fake keys (clean authentication failures from Z.ai and DeepSeek; Used in OpenCode wrote and removed its provider). When the user adds a real account (company page > Add account, or the README recipe over POST /switchy/invoke): choosing Claude Code switches Claude Code to a provider named '<Company> · <account>' whose env carries the key and the plan's host, and Claude Code answers on the plan's models; the card shows the plan's windows (Z.ai and MiniMax 5-hour and weekly, Kimi 5-hour, weekly and monthly, Command Code month's credits plus 5-hour and weekly when window-limited, OpenCode Go 5-hour, weekly and monthly); a DeepSeek, Moonshot or StepFun monitor shows the balance, and spend after a second reading. 'Unexpected balance response' or a parse error means the call's format differs from the documented one. OpenCode Zen's balance is left out until the user decides; it is shown only to the signed-in opencode.ai console.
